label: Sergio Leone / spaghetti Westerns
description: Stylized Western cinema emphasizing landscape, ritualized violence, morally ambiguous gunfighters, and mythic iconography.

label: Le Guin — Earthsea
description: Fantasy cycle centered on names, balance, power, maturation, mortality, and later revision of heroic/gender assumptions.

label: Philip K. Dick — Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
description: SF novel about artificial beings, empathy, unstable reality, commodification, and human identity.

label: Vonnegut — Slaughterhouse-Five
description: Antiwar metafiction blending Dresden, science fiction, fatalism, comedy, trauma, and fragmented time.

label: The Italian Job
description: Heist film organized around planning, specialist roles, machinery, and ensemble execution.

label: Dungeons & Dragons
description: Tabletop role-playing system that systematized fantasy adventuring, classes, dungeons, monsters, progression, and collaborative narrative.

label: Michael Crichton — The Great Train Robbery
description: Historical heist novel centered on specialized planning and execution.

label: Stephen King — The Shining
description: Horror novel combining haunted architecture, addiction/family breakdown, isolation, violence, and psychic sensitivity.

label: Zork
description: Text adventure built around exploration, puzzles, inventory, parser interaction, and dungeon-space imagination.

label: Stephen King — The Stand
description: Post-pandemic epic of social collapse, migration, community formation, good/evil symbolism, and American landscape.

label: Douglas Adams — The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy
description: Comic science fiction combining absurd bureaucracy, cosmic scale, media parody, philosophical jokes, and episodic adventure.

label: Rogue
description: Early procedurally generated dungeon-crawling computer game and namesake of the roguelike tradition.

label: Tanith Lee — The Silver Metal Lover
description: SF novel of a relationship with an artificial person, identity, desire, embodiment, and social control.

label: Stephen King — The Dark Tower
description: Cross-genre quest fusing Western, horror, epic fantasy, metafiction, poetry, and Arthurian resonance.

label: Stephen King/Bachman — The Running Man
description: Dystopian chase narrative built around lethal mass entertainment, inequality, and media spectacle.

label: Atwood — The Handmaid’s Tale
description: Dystopian novel of reproductive control, authoritarian religion, gendered power, memory, and testimony.

label: Larry McMurtry — Lonesome Dove
description: Revisionist Western epic of friendship, aging, violence, myth, migration, and the costs of frontier legend.

label: Cormac McCarthy — Blood Meridian
description: Revisionist anti-Western of scalp-hunting, violence, landscape, history, biblical cadence, and metaphysical terror.

label: William Gibson — Neuromancer
description: Cyberpunk novel crystallizing networked cyberspace, corporate power, body modification, AI, and noir style.

label: Robert Jordan — The Wheel of Time
description: Long-form epic fantasy of cyclical time, prophecy, vast cast, cultures, magic, and world-spanning conflict.

label: Lois Lowry — The Giver
description: Dystopian children’s/YA novel about memory, pain, sameness, choice, family, and managed social stability.

label: Lois Lowry
description: Author whose reflections on memory, loss, childhood, and social choice shaped The Giver.

label: Ultima Online
description: Early mass-market MMORPG emphasizing persistent shared world, skills, economy, social interaction, and emergent play.

label: J. K. Rowling — Harry Potter series
description: School fantasy with hidden magical society, chosen-child structure, mystery plotting, friendship, and escalating war.

label: George R. R. Martin — A Song of Ice and Fire
description: Epic fantasy emphasizing dynastic politics, multiple viewpoints, historical contingency, violence, and skepticism toward heroic conventions.
